pr.title: Hold a pull request in draft while changes for it are built
pr.head: a49718a405a7d95fd3bae0b48d0c30163e7e930f

summary: Projector runs two loops over the operator's pull requests. The review loop reviews each head and, on a pull request the operator wrote, uses draft state as its verdict: publish sets draft state from the newest Projector verdict on the head, whichever model gave it, marking the pull request ready when that verdict is clean and no finding thread is open. The fix loop runs fix-pr to answer the review's findings.

A clean review can still list Suggestions, small improvements that never block. Before this change, fix-pr weighed them on a whim, and nothing kept the pull request from looking ready to merge while fix-pr or the owner built a change that no review had read.

1. fix-pr decides every suggestion. It implements one that is small and clearly right, and defers the rest with a one-line reason in its report.
  2. It holds the pull request while it builds. It posts a hold comment, then marks the pull request draft. The comment is a list of the changes coming, ending in the marker <!-- projector-hold v=1 -->. It deletes the comment once the push that carries them succeeds.
  3. The review side respects the hold. While the pull request's author has a hold open, publish keeps the pull request a draft however clean the newest verdict is, and never approves another author's held pull request. project review status reports held beside the newest verdict. The review watcher watch-prs.sh stops asking for re-reviews until the hold is lifted.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Hold comment: an issue comment by the pull request's author whose body carries <!-- projector-hold v=1 -->. A comment with the marker from anyone else holds nothing.
  • Newest-verdict rule: after each review, publish marks a self-reviewed pull request draft when the head's newest Projector verdict requests changes, a finding thread is open, or the author's hold is open, and ready otherwise.
  • RESPONDED: the review watcher's request to re-review an unchanged head because the author answered without pushing.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• 394c15a: changes requested. One finding: fix-pr marked the pull request draft before it posted the hold, so a watcher pass between the two steps asked for a re-review of an unchanged head.
  • 45ad7a8: clean. fix-pr now posts and reads back the hold before it drafts, and a test checks that order. The finding is resolved.
  • a49718a: clean. A merge of main after #243, which replaced the multi-model sign-off with the newest-verdict rule. The merge carries the hold into that rule.

groups.title: The draft rule reads the hold
groups.kicker: How publish and status learn about a hold, and what they do with it
intro: After each self-review, publish sets draft state from the newest Projector verdict on the head: draft when it requests changes or a finding thread is open, ready otherwise. This group adds the author's hold to that rule. While the hold is open, the pull request stays a draft however clean the newest verdict is.

holds lists hold comments through the REST issue-comments API, reading every page and keeping only the author's. publish adds or held to the draft rule. On a cross-author review it posts a COMMENT rather than an APPROVE while the author holds the pull request. status prefixes its first line with held;, lists each hold, and its JSON gains held and holds. The CLI prints a line saying the hold is what kept a clean head a draft.

files.note: Adds HOLD_MARKER and holds, the hold term in publish's draft rule, the cross-author approval guard, and the held fields status returns.

checks.text: Only the pull request's author can hold it. The login comparison is case-insensitive here, while the watcher compares GitHub's canonical logins exactly.

A held self-review stays a draft under a clean newest verdict, whether it started as a draft or ready. test_the_authors_hold_keeps_a_clean_newest_verdict_a_draft covers both, and the full suite passed (761 tests at a49718a).

A cross-author clean review posts COMMENT while the author's hold is open, and still APPROVEs when only the reviewer posted the marker. test_a_cross_author_review_does_not_approve_while_the_author_holds_the_pull_request covers both.

files.note: Prints why a clean head stayed a draft when the author's hold kept it one.

Tests for the hold under the newest-verdict rule, a stranger's hold, the cross-author approval guard, status output, and the publish message. Two more check that fix-pr, the code, and the watcher agree on the comment, and that fix-pr posts the hold before it drafts.

groups.title: The review watcher waits out a hold
groups.kicker: watch-prs.sh stops asking for re-reviews while a hold is open
intro: watch-prs.sh polls each tracked pull request and prints one line per event. RESPONDED asks for a re-review of an unchanged head, and it fires when a draft has every thread resolved. Before this change, drafting a signed-off pull request was enough to trigger it. The re-review then found the unchanged head clean and marked the pull request ready again.

The GraphQL query now also reads the author and the newest 100 comments, and the row gains a held field. While a hold is open, the watcher records held in its state and announces nothing. When the hold is lifted on a draft, it prints RESPONDED … now that its hold is lifted once, because a review of that head may have run while the hold kept it a draft.

files.note: Adds the author, the comments, and the held field to the query, and the held branch ahead of the RESPONDED test.

checks.text: With the row flag at -, as it is after a clean review marks the pull request ready, a draft without a hold comment prints RESPONDED, and the same draft with the author's hold prints nothing. I checked both by running the watcher through the test suite's fake gh.

files.note: Covers a hold posted before the draft, a hold seen together with a new head, a stranger's marker, and the RESPONDED that drafting before the hold would cause.

groups.title: fix-pr decides suggestions and holds while it builds
groups.kicker: The fix side: what fix-pr implements, and how it posts and lifts the hold
intro: fix-pr answers one pull request's review work. It now treats every suggestion in the newest Projector review of the head, by each model, as a decision to make. It implements a suggestion that is small and clearly right, and defers the rest. An instruction from the owner overrides that default either way.

Before fix-pr builds a suggestion it implements, or a change the owner asks for, it holds the pull request. It posts the hold comment with gh api … -F body=@<file>, reads it back to confirm the marker landed, and only then marks the pull request draft. That order matters: a draft with no hold on an unchanged head looks to the review watcher like an author who answered without pushing, and it would ask for a re-review. fix-pr edits the same comment as more changes come in, keeping the marker on every edit, and deletes it only once the push that carries every change succeeds. It never marks the pull request ready itself; the review of the pushed head does that.

files.note: New sections Decide each suggestion and Hold the pull request while changes are built, plus the hold in the outstanding-work list, the clean conditions, and the report.

checks.text: The hold lands before the draft. Step 1 posts and reads back the comment, and step 2 runs gh pr ready --undo. test_fix_pr_posts_the_hold_before_it_drafts_the_pull_request checks the order in this file, and the watcher test that posts the hold on a ready pull request and then drafts it stays silent on both passes. The full suite passed (761 tests at a49718a).

files.note: Treats a review with Suggestions as work, routes an owner's change to the pull request's subagent, and reports a held pull request or stack layer as not ready.
Requires a skill to cite the new hold section, so the citation checker covers it.
